name: Andalusians
label: Dischord
lede: A bass player from three of D.C.'s more interesting bands picked up the guitar, wrote her own songs on a four-track, and put six of them out on Dischord.

eras.title: A bass player's four-track
eras.text: Basla Andolsun had held down the low end in Del Cielo and Beauty Pill, and played in Justin Moyer's Edie Sedgwick. Andalusians, starting in 2007, was the first band built around her own songs, with a revolving cast of friends filling in the rest.

years.h: [[Basla Andolsun|ca1ce6ba-8758-49b2-b2b0-573e80659fb2]] starts Andalusians, on guitar this time
years.p: Dischord calls Andalusians the songwriting vehicle for Basla Andolsun, bassist in Beauty Pill. The core: Andolsun on vocals and guitar, [[Kristin Forbes|0272f1f9-0965-4fb3-95e3-b8805de18f3a]] on bass, [[Sammy Ponzar|454a79d2-1df8-4d00-84df-3b2aeeb6515c]] on drums.
years.xp:
Basla Andolsun told Creative Loafing she works songs up alone on a four-track first, usually guitar, bass and vocals, then brings them to the band, because a couple of people adding ideas makes the music stronger.

She came to Beauty Pill after Del Cielo, which had recorded with Beauty Pill's Chad Clark at his Silver Sonya studio.

years.p: Dischord lists David Brown on guitar, Chris Farrall on drums and Clark Sabine on bass as regular Andalusians collaborators, live and in the studio, with Chad Molter in the mix too.

eras.title: Do the Work, then take it on the road
eras.text: Andalusians' one Dischord release, Do The Work, came out in early 2009 as a 7-inch with a download card, a very 2009 compromise between vinyl and MP3. Then the band played it in rooms where the cover was five dollars.

years.p: Andalusians' only Dischord release: three songs on the 7-inch, six on the download card, from "Do The Work" to "Single Fantasy." Recorded at Upstairs, mastered by [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] at Silver Sonya, with [[Jean Cook|c304c9c2-e3f3-4abb-b7ca-61f86f4889f5]] on vocals.
years.xp:
Every name from the revolving line-up turns up in the credits: Kristin Forbes and Sammy Ponzar, plus David Brown, Clark Sabine and Chris Farrall. It's a snapshot of a scene where the same dozen people fill each other's bands.

Cleveland Scene heard two sides to Do The Work: an undulating, Gang of Four-like pulse and a gentler Throwing Muses streak, with Basla Andolsun's hiccupping vocals out front.
yt: "Do the Work" and "Turn Off" at Comet Ping Pong

years.h: Basla Andolsun: a bassist playing guitar in Andalusians
years.p: Creative Loafing interviews Basla Andolsun as the Do The Work 7-inch lands. She calls herself a bass player first, even though in Andalusians she mostly plays guitar.
The week Do The Work comes out, Andalusians play a Thursday show at WonderRoot, the Atlanta arts space.

years.h: Andalusians play the Happy Dog in Cleveland for $5
years.p: Andalusians open for the Buried Wires at the Happy Dog on Detroit Avenue in Cleveland, 9 p.m., $5 at the door, still touring Do The Work.
